text.p: Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov, the non pareils of ice dance, took their accustomed position atop the standings when the event began at the world championships on Tuesday.
The reigning Olympic, world and European champions headed team mates Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov with Canadian champions Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz third.

Gritschuk, 26 on Monday, and her 29-year-old partner garnered the best marks of up to 5.9 for their golden waltz and their rumba and are already looking forward to a possible clutch of perfect 6.0 scores in the remaining two phases of the event.
At the European championships in Paris in January they collected six 6.0s for the presentation of their tango, and six more for the artistry of their free dance.
"We didn't expect any today because I don't know if anybody ever got a 6.0 for a compulsory," Gritschuk said. "But we will try to do our best tango and maybe we will get another 6.0."
Pursuing them may be futile for they have been unbeaten in any section since they won the Olympic title in 1994.
But Bourne and Kraatz have not given up the chase, spurred by best marks of 5.8 and 5.8 they received from a Canadian judge.
Some observers felt that smacked of nationalism, but not Bourne and Kraatz.
"I'm more thrilled about that than anything," Bourne said. "It just shows that that judge is an honest judge.
"The top three couples are just so close, so very, very close.
"We all have different styles and it comes down to personal preferences among the judges."
The dances were worth 20 percent of the total marks. The original dance, the tango, on Thursday is worth 30 percent and the free dance on Friday accounts for the remaining 50 percent.
